Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with complaints
of neck pain and stiffness consistent with cervical strain. The mechanism of injury is
plausible for a crash of this type. Over the course of 35 visits, treatment followed a
conventional progression, including manual therapy, stretching, range-of-motion
exercises, and a home exercise program. Symptoms improved steadily, and visit
frequency was reduced accordingly as functional recovery occurred. Examination
revealed reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, which
support the reported injury, while neurological screening, reflexes, and motor
strength remained within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the cervical
spine is known to this provider. Bliling records reflect single, apprporiate charges
for each service rendered without duplication. Patient was discharged to self-directed
home care with instructions to return if symptoms recur.
